author: cskiraly
content:
Catching up on this, so many channels. So there is
- 200Mgas (which is not a direct proportional size increase because of repricing, but it is an increase)
- BAL (which we tend to approx as a 2x, although it largely depends on txs
- PQ signatures (various size targets from 2KB to 8KB per sig), or their ZKP veriant (250 KB etimate).

All these point to a larger payload .... and some point to a larger consensus block. If the BAL is separated, it is still a larger payload and a BAL.

Now on the positive side, here is how SEACAST scales in payload size. This is still not super-optimized. SEACAST allows message-size dependent parametrization. just a quick run.

author: cskiraly
content:
Before you say oh, then 1s is enough for 4MB, I would caution everyone. I see those things in simulations and writeups, but it is not the way to interpret these things. In networking you need headroom, and you need protocols that are elastic (SEACAST is one of those). I could list many reason, but for one, none of you run Linux as an  RTOS I guess. A few interrupts here, an process spiking there, and an app-level forwarder is already not doing its duty as it was in your simulations.

Anyway, we scale nicely, as you can see, and 4MB is absolutely reachable in reasonable time.

author: nashatyrev
content:
Simulated top-layer caching for leanXMSS attestation signatures: peers cache the top layer, so a vote carries only the bottom one (1,204 B instead of 2,404 B). It roughly halves attestation traffic and cuts latency: https://github.com/Nashatyrev/jvm-libp2p/blob/pq-gasper/pq-gasper-top-layer-caching.md

On the protocol side: a full-fledged caching protocol gets complicated quickly (extra topic or req/resp to fetch missing top layers, a queue of pending votes, etc.). I think we can start with something much simpler: each validator sends a full signature every Nth attestation (say every 10th) and the short one otherwise, and nodes just cache what they see. No RPC, no extra state, and it still keeps ~90% of the saving.

Downside: a freshly started node needs ~10 epochs to fill its cache, so until then it can't do a complete job as an aggregator. Attesting itself is not affected.
